schoolPressures.label: Distance
schoolPressures.detail: No functioning secondary school within walking distance; the daily commute to Challakere town is several kilometres.

schoolPressures.label: Harvest labour
schoolPressures.detail: Farm and grazing work during the groundnut harvest and lambing season pulls children away.

schoolPressures.label: Lost grazing land
schoolPressures.detail: Kaval diversion changed herding routines, pulling boys who help move livestock away from regular schooling.

schoolPressures.label: Drought wage work
schoolPressures.detail: In bad years a teenager may do short stretches of daily-wage work while staying on school rolls.

pressures: His 16-year-old son's daily trip to Challakere town costs hours and fare money. The commute is where his schooling is likeliest to break, and his 13-year-old daughter faces the same road next.
In groundnut-harvest and lambing weeks his son is needed in the field or with the flock, so attendance drops in just those weeks.
Herding now means longer walks, so the son who helps move the flock loses school days and the family leans on his labour more.
In a drought year his teenage son earns daily wages while staying on the rolls: he looks enrolled but is missing class, a hidden dropout risk.
factorEffects.sanitation: If his farm household lacks a proper toilet, his adolescent daughter's attendance would suffer first, making an early exit easier to accept.
factorEffects.district: The factor flags the share of English-medium schools in Chitradurga. His own schooling ended at Class 7, and the card shows distance, harvest and herding as what pulls his children out, not language.

changes.factor: % Schools with Furniture available for students
changes.effect: His son, about 16, spends long days at the government high school; without desks and benches, writing and staying through the day is harder.
If his son's school has rooms that need repair, lessons get crowded or cut short, one more strain while harvest and drought work pull at the household.
Where more mothers have ten years of schooling, daughters tend to stay on longer; that could matter for his daughter, about 13, nearing high school.

lag.effect: Chitradurga has one of the lowest shares of English-medium schools in the state, so his children's schooling stays in Kannada; an English-heavy step later could be hard.

schoolPressures.label: Distance & safety
schoolPressures.detail: The nearest Class 9-10 school is several kilometres away, and parents weigh the commute and daughters' safety heavily.

schoolPressures.label: Rearing labour
schoolPressures.detail: Time-bound leaf-feeding and rearing work often falls to daughters, especially when the father is away.

schoolPressures.label: Father's migration
schoolPressures.detail: Seasonal brick-kiln and construction work leaves no one to share the load and disrupts children's attendance.

schoolPressures.label: Hostel seat uncertainty
schoolPressures.detail: Continuing depends on whether a KGBV or similar hostel seat becomes available and how cocoon cycles pay.

pressures: Her daughter, just out of Class 8, faces a several-kilometre trip to a Class 9-10 school. With safety weighing heavily, the commute alone can decide whether she continues.
Leaf-feeding and rearing cannot wait, so the work lands on her 14-year-old daughter, especially when her husband is away. School hours compete directly with the cocoon cycle.
With her husband away on brick-kiln or construction work, nobody shares the load, so both children's attendance bends around her workload.
Her daughter's next step hinges on a hostel seat. If none comes, the household has no other route to Class 9.
factorEffects.sanitation: If her rented-patch household lacks a proper toilet, her daughter's attendance would suffer first once she reaches puberty.
factorEffects.district: The factor flags the share of English-medium schools in Chikkaballapur. The card shows commute, rearing work, her husband's migration and hostel seats as the pressures, not language.

changes.effect: Her son, 15, studies in a government high school; repaired classrooms would keep his lessons running while rearing work pulls at the household.

changes.factor: % Population Living in Households with Improved Sanitation
changes.effect: If her home lacked a toilet, her daughter, 14, would face the safety and privacy worries that can keep older girls at home.
Where more mothers finished ten years of school, families tend to keep daughters in school longer; her daughter's next step, a hostel seat or a long commute, is still open.

lag.factor: % Schools with Furniture available for students
lag.effect: Chikkaballapur ranks near the bottom of Karnataka for desks and benches, so her children could be sitting on the floor through long secondary-school days.
